text:
sam: heads-up — after the continuous-batcher merge tweak we rolled yesterday, prod long-context runs (6k-12k tokens) show steady resident memory growth on KV cache. suspect fragmentation + failed reuse when batches merge, causing HOL stalls and delayed evictions.

anya: do you have a quick repro or flamegraph? can we tell if it’s background reclaim lag or an allocation leak? :thinking:

sam: minimal repro attached below — synthetic stream of 4 concurrent sessions with long prompts, merge window = 50ms. heap profile shows lots of small KV fragments that never coalesce.

jordan: pasting pprof excerpt and a tiny flamegraph snapshot:
```
# pprof top
Samples: 1200 (1000-1500us)
42.5%  kv_cache::fragment_reuse
18.0%  batch_merge::attempt_merge
12.3%  kv_pager::evict_scan
9.8%   kv_cache::alloc_slot
```
flamegraph: wide flat in fragment_reuse -> alloc_slot.

ciara: interesting. maybe when two batches merge we keep separate KV headers and thus fragmentation grows instead of compacting. HOL blocking would keep those fragments pinned until head batch finishes, delaying reclaim.

sam: exact hypothesis. merge path currently does: append other batch blocks' slot refs into head’s vector without re-indexing, so live slot count spikes. eviction is LRU by slot id, but merged slot refs keep older fragments reachable.

anya: can you paste the merge code snippet? I recall we have a fast-path that skips reassembly for perf reasons.

sam: here is the simplified merge sketch:
```
// fast-merge: concat refs, don't reassign slot ownership
head.refs.insert(head.refs.end(), tail.refs.begin(), tail.refs.end());
// mark tail retired, but slots remain referenced by head
```
This avoids O(N) reindexing but leaves many small fragments pointed to by the combined vector.

jordan: that matches the flamegraph. Also saw `kv_pager::evict_scan` timered out more often — pager sees lots of small free ranges, fragmentation prevents large contiguous reuse -> alloc path keeps creating new slabs.

ciara: two immediate mitigations: (A) quick revert to pre-merge behavior for merges that increase refs > threshold, (B) run a background reassembly pass that coalesces adjacent fragments into single slot ids at low priority.

anya: add a third: tune merge window smaller to reduce frequent merges under heavy long-context loads. But that shifts pressure to batch count and latency.

sam: I tried (B) in a local build: background reassembly reduced resident set by ~25% on the synthetic repro, but introduced a small CPU spike.

jordan: can you share the benchmark numbers? curious about tail-latency impact.

sam: repro run summary:
```
baseline (no merge change): rss 7.2GB, p50 latency 28ms, p95 120ms
fast-merge (current): rss 10.1GB, p50 26ms, p95 180ms
fast-merge + bg-reassembly: rss 7.9GB, p50 28ms, p95 140ms
```
so bg-reassembly recovers most memory but latency slightly worse at p95 vs baseline.

ciara: those numbers say the fast-merge is the culprit for memory. But we need a production-safe compromise. I suggest feature-flagging bg-reassembly and a merge threshold gate (skip fast-merge when combined refs > 1024).

anya: agree. also add metrics: fragment_count, avg_fragment_size, merge_ops_skipped. alert if fragment_count rises > X or reclaim rate falls.

jordan: I'll prototype a reassembly that runs incrementally over N slots per tick to avoid big CPU spikes. can we put a cap based on active concurrency?

sam: yes, incremental with a budget works. also adding an eviction hint when reassembly frees contiguous ranges will help the pager.

ciara: action items:
- jordan: prototype incremental reassembly + config for reassembly_budget (due EOD tomorrow)
- sam: add metrics and flag + test matrix for merge_threshold values (in perflab)
- anya: add alert thresholds and runbook note (I’ll draft)

perfbot: created perf-job kv-reassembly-proto in perflab, schedule queued.

sam: thanks. tagging @jordan for ownership. if anyone hits this in staging, add logs: `KV_REASSEMBLY=1` and include `kv_fragment_stats` output.

anya: good triage. also add a short note to the release blockers checklist: if fast-merge enabled, require kv_fragment_metrics in dashboards. :white_check_mark:
